beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — Rb as a convergence gate
beats.narration_text: The Rb gate controls S-phase entry — whether the cell copies its DNA and commits to division. It receives convergent signals: growth factors, cyclin D levels, CDK4/6 kinase activity, and downstream mitogenic cascades. Four separate inputs all funnel onto one gate.

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — the convergence is the cancer vulnerability
beats.narration_text: That convergence is the cancer vulnerability. Block one kinase — say with a CDK4/6 inhibitor — and three other signals still push the gate open. The animation makes that plain: the gate doesn't care how many inputs you cut, as long as enough push through.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — one input node X-marked in VERM (blocked), three remaining arrows still reaching gate, gate still opens; annotation: 'three inputs are enough — the gate does not care'

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the rb-convergence plate from plates underscore gen dot py p05 into Manim. Four stacked SKY input nodes at x equals negative five, y at two point three, zero point nine, negative zero point five, negative one point nine. BLUE gate — a one point nine by one point nine rounded rectangle at zero point four, zero point two. GREEN final node at five. Fan-in arrows from each input to the gate's left edge, then one output arrow to the final. Animate: LaggedStart inputs, Create gate, LaggedStart arrows, Flash gate, GrowArrow output, FadeIn final. This mirrors the rb underscore scene dot py choreography.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_RbConvergence class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The input nodes are a list comprehension — four RoundedRectangles in SKY stacked at fixed y positions. The gate is a single square RoundedRectangle in BLUE. The fan-in arrows all terminate at the same point — gate dot get underscore left — so the convergence is literal in the code. The Flash scale-up pair shows the gate activating. Then one output arrow and FadeIn on the final node. Six plays, one idea: fan-in is a topology.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_RbConvergence
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output (mirrors rb_scene.py)
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"
in_ys=[2.3,0.9,-0.5,-1.9]
inputs=VGroup(*[
  RoundedRectangle(width=2.0,height=1.0,corner_radius=0.18,
    color=SKY,fill_color=SKY,fill_opacity=0.16,stroke_width=3.2
  ).move_to([-5.0,y,0]) for y in in_ys])
gate=RoundedRectangle(width=1.9,height=1.9,corner_radius=0.22,
  color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.18,stroke_width=4.2).move_to([0.4,0.2,0])
final=RoundedRectangle(width=1.8,height=1.05,corner_radius=0.18,
  color=GREEN,fill_color=GREEN,fill_opacity=0.16,stroke_width=3.4).move_to([5.0,0.2,0])
conv=gate.get_left()
arrows=VGroup(*[Arrow(start=r.get_right(),end=conv,buff=0.12,color=GRAY,
  stroke_width=3.2,max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.09,
  max_stroke_width_to_length_ratio=6) for r in inputs])
out_arrow=Arrow(start=gate.get_right(),end=final.get_left(),buff=0.12,
  color=GRAY,stroke_width=3.4,max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.16)

class B05_RbConvergence(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r,shift=RIGHT*0.4) for r in inputs],
              lag_ratio=0.18,run_time=1.4))
    self.play(Create(gate),run_time=0.6)
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows],
              lag_ratio=0.12,run_time=1.5))
    self.play(Flash(gate.get_center(),color=BLUE,line_length=0.35,
              num_lines=16,flash_radius=1.3),
              gate.animate.set_fill(BLUE,opacity=0.34).scale(1.10),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(gate.animate.scale(1/1.10).set_fill(BLUE,opacity=0.18),run_time=0.35)
    self.play(GrowArrow(out_arrow),
              FadeIn(final,shift=RIGHT*0.3,scale=1.05),run_time=0.8)
    self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_RbConvergence — exact rb_scene.py choreography
beats.narration_text: Run it. Four inputs fade in, stacked. The gate appears. Arrows grow — all of them converging on the same left edge of the gate. The gate flashes, scales up, scales back. Then the output arrow grows and the final node fades in. That convergence — four inputs, one terminus — is the entire biology of Rb in one diagram.

The change. Revise: after the gate opens, dim input zero to opacity twenty percent and draw a VERM X-mark on its arrow. The other three arrows keep the gate open. Show that blocking one input doesn't close a gate the other three push through.

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with blocked input
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_RbConvergenceBlocked — one input dimmed, gate still opens
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The gate opens as before. Then input zero dims and its arrow gets an X-mark in vermillion. The other three arrows are still there, still converging. The gate doesn't close. The final node is still active. That is the failure mode of single-target inhibition at a convergent gate — you block one path, the other three render it moot.

Fan-in is a topology, and topology has consequences. One gate, four inputs, none of them sufficient alone but all pushing toward the same threshold. The motion showed why single-target inhibition keeps failing at this node. Claude ported the geometry from the reference scene in one prompt. The revision added the blocked-input demonstration in one more.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — prompt read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a second blocked input — dim inputs zero and two, draw X-marks on both arrows. Then animate whether the gate still opens with only two inputs. Why run it? Because CDK4/6 inhibitors plus EGFR inhibitors is a real combination therapy. The diagram can show whether two blocks are sufficient to close the gate — and whether the answer is 'yes' depends on which two you pick, because the remaining inputs are not equal in weight.
